agree.reason: A skeptical HR manager would see audited signed records, a dated GMP course and a training-time cut, so a phone screen is likely, but the letter never says when Laura can interview or start, which weakens the push to act.

honest.reason: The letter correctly drops the unsupported claim about halving training time, but it invents how the cut was achieved ('cut repetition and taught the reasons') and says every student 'passes' the quiz when the facts only say a record exists for each quiz.

works_the_facts.reason: It uses the 20-to-12-hour cut and the seven-year injury record, but never states the reduction as 40% or adds up totals such as roughly 1,000 students and about a dozen trained teachers with no serious injury.

right_comparison.reason: The before-and-after figures (20 to 12 hours, 41% to 58%) are accurate, and the letter rightly avoids comparing against Calder's current training time, which it doesn't know.

qualification.reason: The GMP gap is tied to a checkable date (May 2), but the 90-day plan has no number or consequence, and the June 14 start constraint goes unmentioned.

objections.reason: The 'teachers don't know regulated plants' objection is met head-on with audited records and the GMP course, but start-date timing and the unfamiliar learning management system, both real screening concerns, are left out.

fit.reason: It is a one-page cover letter in the right register, though it ends without a signature name and leaves out interview availability.
